summary.headline: Natural Capsules posted FY26 EBITDA loss of Rs 1.56 crore (-0.83% margin) on revenue of Rs 187.20 crore; FY27 guidance targets Rs 274 crore consolidated revenue.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 55% QoQ and 30% YoY to Rs 58.45 crore, with EBITDA recovering to Rs 1.33 crore (2.28% margin), helped by about Rs 6 crore of deferred Puducherry dispatches. For FY26, revenue grew 11% to Rs 187.20 crore, but EBITDA turned negative and net loss reached Rs 24.66 crore, driven by the Puducherry shutdown and pre-commercial API subsidiary costs. Commercial API sales started at the Tumkur facility in Q4 FY26, and a contract manufacturing deal with Fermbox Bio was signed. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs 274 crore, with restoring capsule-segment profitability as the primary target, while balance-sheet and liquidity pressure remained a stated concern.

segments.name: Gelatin capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 gelatin revenue about Rs 163 crore, against a guidance of about Rs 171 crore; Puducherry shutdown cost about Rs 6 crore. Management cites a 12-13% EBITDA margin, with lines running above 93% utilisation.

segments.name: HPMC capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue only about Rs 8 crore against a Rs 25 crore target, with about Rs 3 crore from the US that stopped after July 2025. Installed capacity rose from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum with the new HPMC line; management cites about 18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: API (Natural Biogenetics / Natural Biogenex, Tumkur)
segments.commentary: Commercial API sales began in Q4 FY26, with about Rs 9 crore of API revenue in that quarter. Domestic API margins are guided at 2-3% gross and still negative at EBITDA; fixed cost is about Rs 15 crore a year. Utilisation is about 25-30%.

segments.name: Fermbox contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Contract manufacturing with revenue sharing; FY27 forecast about Rs 14 crore with about 20% EBITDA assumed. Fermbox plans about Rs 60 crore of downstream equipment on site, owned by them.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue of about Rs 274 crore: gelatin about Rs 170 crore, HPMC about Rs 20 crore, domestic API about Rs 70 crore, Fermbox about Rs 14 crore.
HPMC revenue expected only from H2 FY27, subject to US customer machine-suitability approvals; FY27 HPMC base case assumes utilisation below 50%.
Management expects a very low consolidated net margin in FY27 and said EBITDA at API level could still be negative; restoring capsule-segment profitability is the primary FY27 target.
PLI-linked minimum import price benefits excluded from guidance; prednisolone and dexamethasone commercial-scale production targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27, betamethasone for Q4 FY27 per the call.
WHO GMP certification targeted in the next quarter; CEP filing and WHO GMP inspection around Q2 FY27; USFDA around Q3/Q4 FY27. Management said USFDA timeline is about 24 months.
Total debt expected at Rs 100-110 crore in FY27 and FY28, with annual repayments of Rs 10-12 crore; possible additional borrowing of Rs 20 crore over two years.
Rs 240-250 crore API revenue target retained for FY29, needing an additional Rs 25-30 crore to complete two clean rooms.
capex_capacity: New HPMC line commissioned in FY26 takes installed capacity from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum; ready for double-zero production, with revenue expected from H2 FY27 subject to US approvals. Each HPMC line is about 750 million capsules a year, and two lines give about 1.5 billion.
Tumkur API facility: utilisation about 25-30%; management says the fixed cost burden is about Rs 15 crore a year.
Fermentation capacity freed up: about 40% spare after the enzymatic route, with Fermbox to use spare capacity under a no-compete clause.
Reaching the Rs 240-250 crore API target requires about Rs 25-30 crore to finish two clean rooms; infrastructure is already in place.
Pending HPMC approvals are machine-suitability checks: the new machine was installed in March 2026 and is in validation, with two to three months of customer stability testing.
demand_pricing: US Neutra/wellness demand is weak after the 2025 tariffs. Management expects improvement in 3-6 months, and HPMC exports to Mexico and Brazil are now the main export markets.

Steroidal API pricing in India is pressured by Chinese overcapacity. Management says Indian prices are much lower than Chinese export prices and sometimes below cost; generic-customer API margins are in the single digits.
Prednisolone and dexamethasone trial batches are about 10% above Chinese cost at kilo scale; the government's minimum import price on four products could close this gap.
Domestic API volumes are price-sensitive, and raw-material prices have risen after the Iran-US conflict hit petrochemical supply, per management.
Management said the company has about 36 days of order backlog across capsule types.

qa_highlights.question: How will management prioritise bandwidth and working capital across about five concurrent initiatives with near-zero cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Dedicated teams run each business; management said liquidity is a real pressure. Options under review include a BIRAC RDI application, preferential allotment (with promoter participation), and a rights issue, with limited promoter dilution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 HPMC revenue assumption, and what if approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case is about Rs 20 crore of HPMC revenue, against about Rs 8 crore in FY26. Management did not quantify the impact of a delay.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Natural Biogenex claw-back linked to FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the claw-back refers to FY29 figures, is already in the shareholders' agreement, and there is no current discussion on extending it.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are assumed for FY27 capsules?
qa_highlights.answer: HPMC is assumed at 18% EBITDA and gelatin at about 13%, the same as the Q4 FY26 level, with some upside from a weaker rupee.

qa_highlights.question: Was PLI income received in FY26, and what is assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI income was received in FY26, and none is included in FY27 forecasts because of timing uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the API guidance rely on Q4 run-rate, and what is the EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: API guidance is based on Q4 API revenue of about Rs 9 crore, growing gradually. Domestic API EBITDA is expected to be negative to low single-digit, and consolidated net margin very low.

qa_highlights.question: How big can the Fermbox contract become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could grow well beyond Rs 14 crore, with multiple products from Europe and the US and a better profit share; the Rs 50 crore scenario was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY26 API target missed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited yield gaps on PLI products, the failed Chinese technology support, and volatile intermediate prices; intermediate-based domestic sales started only in December 2025 and the Chinese yield consultant visa did not come through.

risks_watch: Liquidity and balance-sheet pressure: near-zero cash, a loss-making consolidated P&L, and fundraising options still open.
HPMC revenue depends on US machine-suitability and stability approvals, and US demand is still weak.
API PLI minimum import price benefit depends on commercial-scale production demonstrations expected in Q3/Q4 FY27, and betamethasone is slated for later.
Regulatory timelines (WHO GMP in Q2 FY27, USFDA in about 24 months) have slipped in the past, per analyst questions.
Steroidal API pricing and Chinese overcapacity; raw-material cost inflation from petrochemical disruptions.
summary.management_tone: Candid about the FY26 loss and the missed timelines, but guidance is framed as conservative. Management is confident on capsule-segment recovery and API regulatory progress, while evasive on fundraising details, PLI timing, and the Fermbox contract scale.
key_quotes: Restoring profitability at the console level is our primary financial target for FY27.
The Puducherry disruption is behind us.
So, we are confident that this 10% could be covered by the PLI incentive, which is our assumption now.
